title: Launch Gates & Metrics Inventory
content: Purpose: Single-source, compact inventory of launch gates, primary KPIs, thresholds for 'go/no-go', and the minimal monitoring bundle required during first 72 hours. Meant for product-ops, PM, SRE, and release engineering to use during pre-flight and canary phases.

Scope: Applies to API feature launches (new route or significant behavior change) and Dedicated/Dedicated+Private rollout variants. Not intended for experimental A/B UX tests unless they affect inference routing or cost metrics.

Summary dashboard (one-line): Primary KPI = P50 latency (ms), Secondary KPI = 99th-percentile error rate (% of requests returning 5xx or incomplete streaming), Cost KPI = tokens-per-second per-GPU and estimated cost-per-100k-requests. Acceptance thresholds are listed per gate below.
Launch gates overview: We break readiness into five gates. Each gate has an owner and absolute exit criteria. Gate names are intentionally minimal to reduce ceremony.

Gate 0 — Concept & Risk Triage (owner: PM) — Exit criteria: documented user story + top-3 risks identified + essential compliance checklist (data path & PII review) complete. Signals: design doc linked and accepted by security. KPI impact: N/A.

Gate 1 — Engineering Feasibility & Perf Baseline (owner: Eng lead) — Exit criteria: prototype passes perf microbenchmarks on representative load. Baseline metrics: P50 latency <= 120ms for dev-2 tokens workload; mem/KV cache hit-rate >= 70%. Failure condition: >20% regression vs baseline or any model OOM on targeted GPU type.

Gate 2 — End-to-end Staging Validation (owner: QA lead) — Exit criteria: integration tests green, SLO smoke tests passing, canary harness configured. KPIs: P50 latency <= 150ms; p95 latency <= 450ms; error-rate <= 0.5% on staging workload. Must have synthetic traffic replay + golden prompt set baseline.

Gate 3 — Canary & Observability (owner: SRE) — Exit criteria: 48h canary at target traffic share (min 5%) with no critical alerts. KPIs: 99th-percentile latency trend < +20% vs staging; error-rate sustained < 1%; no sustained increase in cost-per-token > 15%. Observability: traces + token-level cost breakdown + KV cache metrics must be live.

Gate 4 — Global Rollout (owner: Product Ops) — Exit criteria: canary acceptance, automated rollback policy configured, runbook & on-call rotation set for first 72h. KPIs for go: p50 latency within target SLA, weekly growth deviation alerts, and no blocking security findings.
KPI definitions (canonical):
- P50 latency: median server-side time from request receive to first byte of model output (ms).
- P95/P99 latency: same as above for 95th/99th percentiles. Use 5-minute sliding windows for alerts during canary.
- Error-rate: fraction of requests returning HTTP 5xx, model runtime OOM, or truncated streaming due to server-side error. Countdown windows: 1m, 5m, 1h.
- Cost-per-100k-requests: includes GPU time estimate + egress + infra overhead. Use simulated token distributions matching production prompts.
- KV cache hit-rate: percent of requests serviced from cached KV prefixes; tracked at request and token granularity.
Monitoring & alerting baseline (what must be in place before Gate 3):
- Dashboards: latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate, request volume by route, tokens/sec per-GPU, cost-estimate per-minute.
- Alerts: p99 latency > baseline *1.5 for 5m; error-rate > 1% for 5m; queue/backpressure > 30s.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces with span tags for model variant, routing decision, and cache hit/miss. Retention: 7d for initial rollout window.
Canary plan (practical):
- Duration: Nominal 48 hours, extendable to 7 days if noisy signals occur.
- Traffic ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% (each step min 4 hours, contingent on green metrics).
- Canary synthetic checks: golden-prompt quality scoring (BLEU/semantic similarity), hallucination probe set, and throughput stress test run at 1.5x expected peak.
- Rollback criteria: any of the following sustained for 15m: p99 latency spike >2x baseline, error-rate >2%, or critical customer-impacting SLO breach reported by on-call.
Post-launch monitoring (first 72h checklist):
- 15-minute incident triage rotation: product-ops + SRE + ENG on-call.
- Hourly snapshot summary to stakeholders: traffic, latency, error-rate, cost burn-rate.
- Runbook actions: cache warmup guidance, emergency model-variant fallback plan, circuit-breaker thresholds and how to toggle.
Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Unexpected model degradation in certain prompt slices. Mitigation: holdback set of prompts & auto-eval on every deploy. Owner: Research.
- Risk: Cost overruns due to token distribution mismatch. Mitigation: conservative quota + preflight cost sim. Owner: Finance.
- Risk: Cross-tenant data leakage in private deployment. Mitigation: separate KMS keys + audit logs + pen-test. Owner: Security.
Action items (short):
- Daniel: finalize canary traffic gating automation (due 2026-02-25).
- María: add golden-prompt set to synthetic runner and define quality threshold (due 2026-02-22).
- Ethan: instrument token-level cost breakdown in staging and wire to dashboard (due 2026-02-24).
Open questions (for next sync):
- What is the minimum acceptable cache hit-rate for the dedicated SKU during high burst traffic?
- Do we require legal sign-off for samples used in golden prompts for non-production telemetry?
Notes & references:
- Refer to the 'go-to-prod' docs for Dedicated SKU sizing assumptions (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- This sheet intentionally keeps gates tight and actionable; if a gate fails, the default is to pause rollout and debrief within 2 hours.
Next steps: gather sign-offs for gates 1–3, finalize alert thresholds with SRE, and schedule a dry run (staging->canary) during low-traffic window. Owner for next steps: Product Ops (Aisha).
